title: Everlight: Vale of Echoes
subtitle: The Crown of Roads
premise: The shattered Everlight Ways are being forced awake by Lord Vael Corven. The player is not a chosen heir: they become important by deciding who may use the restored roads, what communities receive their power, and whether the network should be free, governed, or silenced.

timeModel.measurement: First-play estimate with ordinary exploration, required combat retries, dialogue, and travel after early fast-travel unlock; optional side quests, property optimization, recurring world events, and postgame are excluded from the 32.5-hour main total.

campaignRules.lightDeathPenalty: Respawn at the most recent waystone or safe camp, keep story and quest state, and lose at most ten percent of carried unbanked gold capped by chapter.
campaignRules.factionPolicy: The player may earn early ranks in every faction. Two late rival gates are mutually exclusive for capstone ranks and rewards, but no choice blocks the critical path.
campaignRules.bossPolicy: Every required boss supports viable melee, ranged, magic, hybrid, defensive, and companion-assisted solutions. Preparation changes difficulty but never supplies a mandatory single counter.
campaignRules.economyPolicy: Property ownership accelerates upgrades, vehicles, and optional projects but is never required to finish the campaign. All income resolves through in-game days and the central ledger.
campaignRules.companionPolicy: Mira is recruited by the story. All other companions are optional, remain available after their introduction, and no critical-path objective requires one named companion.
campaignRules.eventPolicy: Recurring in-game world events enrich pacing and rewards but cannot expire essential story content or permanently destroy owned assets.

acts.title: The Vale Wakes
acts.dramaticQuestion: Why are the Ways waking, and what did the first awakened road ask of the player?

acts.title: Roads of the Broken Kingdoms
acts.dramaticQuestion: Can the regions cooperate before Corven turns restoration into control?

acts.title: The Crown of Roads
acts.dramaticQuestion: Who should govern the restored network, and what cost will the player accept to reach the Spire?

acts.title: The Last Echo
acts.dramaticQuestion: Will the Everlight become a public road, a guarded trust, a single ruler's instrument, or a sleeping power once more?

npcs.name: Mira Vale
npcs.arc: Her missing survey team and distrust of institutions force her to decide whether hope can be organized without becoming control.

npcs.name: Elya
npcs.arc: A name erased from Moonfall's records may be hers, or may belong to the intelligence speaking through her spells.

npcs.name: Torren Pike
npcs.arc: A former road captain must choose between protecting people and protecting the institution that failed them.

npcs.name: Rennic
npcs.arc: A sea-beast that follows his trail is guarding the truth about the expedition he abandoned.

npcs.name: Ves
npcs.arc: Every favor has a price until the player gives Ves a reason to choose loyalty without leverage.

npcs.name: Lord Vael Corven
npcs.arc: Corven is correct that Aeralis is fragmenting, but believes only centralized control can save it. He becomes the warning at the heart of every player choice.

npcs.name: Nym
npcs.arc: Nym's growing personhood reveals that the Ways remember their users and that the Last Guardian is made from accumulated human choices.

npcs.name: Reeve Elowen Reed
npcs.arc: She wants prosperity without selling Briarwatch's future to the first powerful patron.

npcs.name: Fenra Quill
npcs.arc: A hard-nosed broker who quietly structures local ownership to prevent absentee rule.

npcs.name: Daren Anvil
npcs.arc: His failing forge becomes the player's first proof that investment can change a town.

npcs.name: Iona Greenbottle
npcs.arc: She tracks how the returning Ways alter plants, medicine, and monsters.

npcs.name: Rook Alder
npcs.arc: He teaches that a mount is a partner and traversal tool, not a speed tax.

npcs.name: Curator Lio Senn
npcs.arc: Lio values preservation so fiercely that living communities can become secondary to the record.

npcs.name: Captain Arven Holt
npcs.arc: Arven protects the roads, but his answer to dangerous magic is increasingly indiscriminate.

npcs.name: Ash-Magister Selka
npcs.arc: Selka believes risky knowledge is safer in trained hands than buried, and repeatedly tests the limits of that belief.

npcs.name: Oren Valegold
npcs.arc: Oren can mobilize resources faster than any council, but always expects ownership in return.

npcs.name: Captain Iri Cloudwake
npcs.arc: Iri wants the sky to remain open and will support any ending that prevents a monopoly on travel.

npcs.name: Bryn Coil
npcs.arc: A brilliant mechanic afraid of heights builds the machine that forces her to face the open sky.

npcs.name: Regent Solvi Aster
npcs.arc: Solvi must decide whether inherited stewardship is service or merely a polished form of possession.

npcs.name: Aurelion, Last Guardian
npcs.arc: Aurelion preserves the intentions of countless former users and can become partner, prison, or enemy depending on the player's proof.

bosses.name: Hollow Warden
bosses.arena: Circular seal chamber with pillars and a breakable outer ring.

solutions.melee: Parry or dodge through sweeps and punish the exposed core.
solutions.ranged: Use pillars to break charge lines and attack after impacts.
solutions.magic: Ward the radial burst or detonate runes at range.
solutions.companion: Interrupt summons and create a revive window.

bosses.name: Stormbound Knight
bosses.arena: Observatory bridge with grounded shelters and rotating lightning rods.

solutions.melee: Stay inside lance reach, counter shield turns, and use shelters during overcharge.
solutions.ranged: Redirect rods and punish aerial recovery.
solutions.magic: Ground lightning into charged sigils or barrier the pulse.
solutions.companion: Order an interrupt while repositioning between shelters.

bosses.name: Bellowsaint Rusk, the Cinder Maw
bosses.arena: Flooded forge with cooling sluices, anvils, and safe high ground.

solutions.melee: Break leg armor, use anvils as cover, and punish cooled vents.
solutions.ranged: Trigger sluices and target vents from the catwalk.
solutions.magic: Use any control or barrier school to survive heat waves; no ice spell is required.
solutions.companion: Torren can hold aggro, while any companion can activate a distant sluice.

bosses.name: Pearlback Leviathan
bosses.arena: Skiff pursuit into broken Tidemirror platforms and a final sheltered cove.

solutions.melee: Board exposed shell plates and strike anchors during close passes.
solutions.ranged: Hit glowing barnacles and rigging targets during the pursuit.
solutions.magic: Ward the sonic burst and overload tide mirrors from shore.
solutions.companion: Navigator companions shorten pursuit hazards; others protect the skiff or expose weak points.

bosses.name: The Crownstep Regent
bosses.arena: A terraced storm court whose three anchors can be disabled in any order.

solutions.melee: Ride wind lanes into close-range stagger opportunities.
solutions.ranged: Break exposed anchor relays from safe terraces.
solutions.magic: Reverse tethers or protect a terrace with zones and barriers.
solutions.companion: Assign a companion to delay one anchor while fighting another.

bosses.name: The Last Guardian
bosses.arena: A floating Waystation that rearranges between offense, traversal, and memory phases.

solutions.melee: Chain platform launches and counter the guardian's mirrored weapon.
solutions.ranged: Control remote relays and break constellations before they converge.
solutions.magic: Attune matching runes or brute-force them with sustained resource management.
solutions.companion: High bond converts one memory attack into an assist; low bond remains fully winnable.

bosses.name: Lord Vael Corven
bosses.arena: Meridian Spire ascends through duel floor, collapsing lattice, and open-sky crown.

solutions.melee: Read stance changes, counter his duel strings, and use lattice gaps as punish windows.
solutions.ranged: Maintain angles, interrupt relay captures, and punish channel recovery.
solutions.magic: Contest hazards with zones, wards, summons, or resource burst without a required element.
solutions.companion: All recruited companions provide distinct support, but solo completion remains viable.

solutions.melee: Cut summon vines and stay beneath antler sweeps.
solutions.ranged: Break crown buds before the charge.
solutions.magic: Clear roots with damage, control, or wards.

solutions.melee: Deflect shard volleys and punish after wall impacts.
solutions.ranged: Break antler crystals while kiting through cover.
solutions.magic: Shatter reflections with any burst or disrupt them with control.
solutions.companion: A companion can bait one mirrored charge.

bosses.name: The Unmoored Star
bosses.arena: A zero-gravity hollow reached only by a fully upgraded airship.

solutions.melee: Use gravity wells to close distance and counter starblade arcs.
solutions.ranged: Pin orbiting shards before they form constellations.
solutions.magic: Stabilize or exploit gravity phases with several spell schools.
solutions.companion: Bond capstones change assist patterns, not access or victory conditions.

endings.requirement: High public trust and at least two Grand Waystations restored through public or neutral methods.
endings.result: The Ways operate as a commons with regional councils and Skyfarer transit guarantees.

endings.requirement: Three or more allied factions or strong neutral coalition support.
endings.result: A rotating coalition governs the lattice with explicit checks and companion oversight.

endings.requirement: Primary faction capstone and chartered airship.
endings.result: One faction leads restoration; benefits and costs reflect its ideology and the player's prior restraints.
The continental lattice is dismantled while local nodes remain, protecting autonomy at the cost of slower recovery.

endings.requirement: Any campaign state; Nym or Aurelion truth adds a consent-aware variant.
endings.result: The Ways sleep until communities are prepared, preserving the mystery and preventing immediate central control.

endingEvaluation.noGoldenEndingRule: Every ending preserves something and sacrifices something; preparation improves outcomes but never produces a consequence-free perfect state.
